lines.text: Many learners say: Let's take a coffee after class.
Better: Let's have a coffee after class.
We have coffee, we do not take it.
The second! Let's have a beer tonight.

data.wrong: Let's take a coffee after class.
data.right: Let's have a coffee after class.
data.why: We have coffee, we do not take it.

native.tip: Para tomar um café ou uma bebida, o inglês usa “have”: “have a coffee”.

en.tip: For a coffee or a drink, English uses “have”: “have a coffee”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “Let's take a coffee after class.” The right way is “Let's have a coffee after class.” In Portuguese we say “tomar um café”, but in English you “have” a coffee. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
